claim.markdown_says: '## D.14.2.3 Class test for characters in a particular alphabet.' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44744) and '## D.14.3 Culturally-adaptable applications' (:44774) - whereas the siblings transcribed on p1112 are '#### D.14.2.1 General' (:44705) and '#### D.14.2.2 Currency string and currency symbol' (:44714), under '### D.14.2 Culturally-specific applications' (:44702) and '### D.14.1 General' (:44693), all under '## D.14 Culturally-specific, culturally-adaptable, and multilingual applications' (:44690).
claim.why_it_matters: This is the sharpest instance of the promotion pattern in the batch: D.14.2.3 is a third-level subclause whose own two immediate siblings are correctly at '####', yet it is emitted at '##' - the same level as the top-level clause D.14 - so an outline built from the markdown shows D.14.2.3 leaving D.14.2 and standing beside D.14, and D.14.3 leaving D.14 entirely. Because D.14.2.1/.2 ARE correct here, the inconsistency is internal to one page pair and cannot be explained away as a uniform flattening convention. It also directly contradicts the nesting the standard's own numbering states.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. The claim quotes both sources accurately, but every inference drawn from those quotes fails. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind is 'missing-heading', yet both headings are present in the markdown verbatim, complete, and correctly numbered: page-1113.md:11 '## D.14.2.3 Class test for characters in a particular alphabet.' (period included, matching the PDF's printed trailing period) and :41 '## D.14.3 Culturally-adaptable applications'. Every word of both headings, and the whole body between them, matches the render character-for-character. The dispute is purely over how many '#' characters precede text that is fully and correctly transcribed. (2) THE PDF CARRIES NO DEPTH CUE TO LOSE. I pulled the span metrics with PyMuPDF from 'specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.pdf'. On PDF page 1112 the five headings D.14, D.14.1, D.14.2, D.14.2.1, D.14.2.2 are ALL Cambria,Bold size=11.67 at x0=63.5 - identical font, identical size, identical left margin, zero indent step. On page 1113 D.14.2.3 (y0=191.4), D.14.3 (y0=570.7) and D.14.3.1 (y0=596.0) are likewise ALL Cambria,Bold size=11.67 at x0=80.0 (80.0 vs 63.5 is only the recto/verso margin difference - the running header shifts identically). The 300dpi renders confirm it visually: a top-level clause heading (D.14) and a fourth-level one (D.14.2.2) are typographically indistinguishable. So the claim's premise - that the PDF 'prints D.14.2.3 at the same clause depth as its siblings' in a way the markdown contradicts - is inverted: the PDF prints ALL of D.14 through D.14.3.1 at the SAME visual depth, and the only depth signal the PDF carries is the printed clause number itself, which the markdown reproduces exactly. A literal typographic transcription would put all eight headings at one level. (3) THE 'INTERNAL TO ONE PAGE PAIR' ARGUMENT IS FALSE AT DOCUMENT SCALE. Cross-tabulating numbering depth against '#' count over all of specs/ISO_COBOL.md: depth-2 headings appear as 198x '##' and 37x '###'; depth-3 as 347x '##', 539x '###', 19x '####'; depth-4 as 241x '##', 668x '###', 32x '####'; depth-5 as 144x '##', 151x '###', 43x '####'. D.14.2.3 at '##' is one of 241 depth-4 headings at '##' (26% of them); D.14.3 at '##' is one of 347 depth-3 headings at '##' (38%). There is no document-wide convention for D.14.2.3 to violate - the '#' count is not a faithful channel anywhere in this transcription, so a locally-correct '####' on D.14.2.1/.2 is coincidence, not a rule. (4) THE OUTLINE ARGUMENT SELF-DESTRUCTS. The markdown injects page furniture as headings: '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' 942 times at level 1 and '## Page NNNN' 1233 times at level 2. Any outline derived from '#' counts is already reset at essentially every page boundary. D.14.2.3 at '##' is not rendered 'beside D.14' - it sits beside '## Page 1113' three lines above it. The hash hierarchy conveys no document structure to corrupt. CONCLUSION: no text, no glyph, no choice indicator and no meaning differs between the PDF and the markdown on this page. This is markdown formatting noise in a channel the PDF never populated, not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. Incidental note, NOT a discrepancy: the PDF itself is defective here - the body under 'D.14.2.3 Class test for characters in a particular alphabet.' opens 'To define a multiple-character currency string, the CURRENCY SIGN clause...', which belongs to D.14.2.2. The markdown transcribes ISO's own defect faithfully, which is the correct behavior for a transcription.
verdict.corrected_description: No content discrepancy. Both headings are transcribed verbatim and correctly numbered; only the markdown '#' depth differs, and the PDF encodes no heading depth at all (every heading on pages 1112-1113, from top-level D.14 to fourth-level D.14.2.3, is Cambria,Bold 11.67pt at one common left margin). The '#'-count irregularity is document-wide, not local - 241 of 941 depth-4 headings and 347 of 905 depth-3 headings across specs/ISO_COBOL.md sit at '##' - and the markdown's level 1 and 2 slots are consumed by 942 running-header and 1233 page-marker pseudo-headings, so no usable outline exists to be broken. If the project wants a machine-readable clause tree, it must be derived from the printed clause numbers (which are intact), not from '#' counts; that is a transcription-wide normalization task, not a page-1113 finding.
